correctness.rationale: For each nonnegative feasible core, weighted spatial and velocity marginals belong to the respective fixed column spaces, and positive mass normalizes the velocity marginal to the prescribed barycenter. Conversely their outer product gives a rank-one matrix with exact positive mass and momentum. Linear independence of active constraint columns yields the sharp polytope vertex support bound; the codimension-one vertex list follows by solving two equations and classifying all sign patterns. Minimal one-direction completion follows by appending a positive spatial vector or any weighted nonnegative velocity distribution with the target physically admissible mean. The three-velocity example and exact finite checker corroborate but do not replace the universal proof. Boundary cases empty cones, zero-coordinate supports, nonunit weights and arbitrary core rank are explicitly included.

value.rationale: The motivating corrected-core quadratic optimization can have an empty feasible set even when mass and momentum are physically admissible. This theorem completely characterizes feasibility, reduces a joint r-squared core test to two smaller independent LPs, and constructs a minimal one-direction repair. An exact three-node example demonstrates the obstruction despite constant and velocity factors already present. The result is a natural structural design guarantee rather than routine parameter substitution.
